## Load packages

```{r message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
if (!requireNamespace("caret", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("caret")
if (!requireNamespace("randomForest", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("randomForest")

library(caret)
library(randomForest)

banknote <- read.csv("banknote.csv")

# Remove missing values if any
banknote <- na.omit(banknote)

# Convert response to factor for classification
banknote$class <- factor(banknote$class, levels = c(0, 1))

# Check data structure
str(banknote)
summary(banknote)
```

Q1
```{r}
set.seed(123)
train_index <- createDataPartition(banknote$class, p = 0.75, list = FALSE)

train.data <- banknote[train_index, ]
test.data  <- banknote[-train_index, ]

nrow(train.data)
nrow(test.data)
prop.table(table(train.data$class))
prop.table(table(test.data$class))
```

Q2
```{r}
set.seed(123)

tune_result <- tuneRF(
  x = train.data[, setdiff(names(train.data), "class")],
  y = train.data$class,
  stepFactor = 1,
  improve = 0.01,
  trace = TRUE,
  plot = FALSE
)

tune_result
best_mtry <- tune_result[which.min(tune_result[, 2]), 1]
best_mtry
# Every split in each tree
# randomly select 2 predictors for candicates

set.seed(123)

rf_model <- randomForest(
  class ~ .,
  data = train.data,
  mtry = best_mtry,
  importance = TRUE
)

rf_model

# OOB confusion matrix
oob_conf <- rf_model$confusion
oob_conf

oob_cm <- oob_conf[, 1:2]
TP <- oob_cm["1", "1"]   # forged predicted as forged
FN <- oob_cm["1", "0"]   # forged predicted as genuine
TN <- oob_cm["0", "0"]   # genuine predicted as genuine
FP <- oob_cm["0", "1"]   # genuine predicted as forged

oob_sensitivity <- TP / (TP + FN)
oob_specificity <- TN / (TN + FP)
oob_accuracy <- (TP + TN) / sum(oob_cm)

oob_sensitivity
oob_specificity
oob_accuracy
```

Q3
```{r}
test_pred <- predict(rf_model, newdata = test.data)

test_cm <- confusionMatrix(test_pred, test.data$class, positive = "1")
test_cm

test_cm$table

test_sensitivity <- test_cm$byClass["Sensitivity"]
test_specificity <- test_cm$byClass["Specificity"]
test_accuracy <- test_cm$overall["Accuracy"]

test_sensitivity
test_specificity
test_accuracy
```

Q4
```{r}
varImpPlot(rf_model, type = 1, main = "Variable Importance: MeanDecreaseAccuracy")
# MeanDecreaseAccuracy measures how much the prediction accuracy decreases when a variable is permuted or excluded. A larger value indicates a more important variable.

varImpPlot(rf_model, type = 2, main = "Variable Importance: MeanDecreaseGini")
# MeanDecreaseGini measures how much a variable contributes to decreasing node impurity across the forest. A larger value indicates a more important variable for classification splits.
```

Q5
```{r}
mda <- randomForest::importance(rf_model, type = 1)[, "MeanDecreaseAccuracy"]
mda

mda_pct <- 100 * mda / sum(mda)
mda_pct <- round(mda_pct, 2)
mda_pct

importance_percent <- data.frame(
  Variable = names(mda_pct),
  MeanDecreaseAccuracy = round(mda, 4),
  Percentage = mda_pct
)

importance_percent[order(-importance_percent$Percentage), ]
# The table above shows the importance of each variable based on MeanDecreaseAccuracy, expressed as a percentage of the total importance.
```

Q6

For classification problems in random forest, a common default is:
mtry = sqrt(p), where p is the number of predictors
```{r}
sqrt(25)
```
